title: Arrival
events_chronological: Twelve alien vessels appear at points around the Earth and the world's militaries mobilise.
Colonel Weber recruits linguist Louise Banks to translate the heptapods' language at the Montana landing site.
Louise and physicist Ian Donnelly enter the shell and make contact through the barrier with the two heptapods they nickname Abbott and Costello.
Louise takes off her hazmat suit to show the aliens a human face, and the two sides begin building a vocabulary out of written logograms.
As Louise learns the circular written language she starts having vivid, unplaceable visions of a daughter.
The twelve sites share their findings until China's translation of the phrase "use weapon" fractures the coalition and the exchanges stop.
Rogue soldiers plant a bomb inside the Montana shell while Louise and Ian are working in it.
Abbott shields the two humans from the blast and is fatally injured, and the shell withdraws out of reach.
Nations pull out one by one, China issues an ultimatum, and the Montana camp is ordered to evacuate.
Louise is lifted alone into the shell, where Costello explains that the weapon is the language itself and that the heptapods have come because in three thousand years they will need humanity's help.
Louise understands that learning the language has unmoored her from linear time and that her visions are memories of a future.
In one such vision Louise sees herself at a United Nations gala being thanked in private by General Shang of China.
Using what the vision showed her, Louise phones Shang's private number in the present and recites his dying wife's words, and he stands down the Chinese fleet.
The other nations follow, the coalition re-forms, and the twelve shells rise and vanish.
Ian tells Louise he is amazed by her, and she chooses to have the child with him knowing exactly how it will end.
Louise and Ian's daughter Hannah is born and grows up, and Louise plays with her and teaches her words.
Hannah is diagnosed with an incurable illness, and Louise tells her that her father walked out after she told him something he could not accept.
Hannah dies in hospital with Louise holding her.
syuzhet_notes: Told-order bullets 1, 2 and 12 are presented as flashbacks to a dead child and a broken marriage, and the film's central move is to establish at told-order bullets 14-15 that they are flash-forwards - memories of a future Louise has not yet lived. Told-order bullet 15 is a vision of an event that lies ahead of bullet 16, so the phone call that saves the situation is caused by its own consequence.
fabula_notes: Placing Hannah's birth, illness and death after the arrival is the reading the ending establishes; on a first viewing they are framed as the past. Ian's eventual departure is stated by Louise to Hannah rather than shown, and the years between the shells leaving and Hannah's death are compressed.
